text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Ruling coalition offers compromise deal to opposition Social Democrats in attempt to push through at least part of its tax reform project.
- High water still threatens Oderbruch region of eastern Germany.
- Dollar reaches highest level against the mark since November 1989.
- Employers demand cuts in social insurance payments.
- Retailers say they are satisfied with trade on first day of annual end-of-summer sales.
HANDELSBLATT
- Potential investors shy away from Oderbruch region due to floods.
- Coalition sources say government and opposition could do a deal to cut top rate of income tax to 45 percent.
- German government warns against delay in Europe's planned single currency.
- Latest data points to continuing recovery in east German economy until autumn this year.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Ruling coalition ready for compromise with opposition in tax policy.
- Dieter Schulte, head of German Trade Union Federation (DGB), raises prospect of a 25-hour working week.
- Consumers associations agree dangerous products should be withdrawn from the market more quickly than at present.
- Court rules that travel agents must tell customers about the cheapest possible airport when they are booking a flight.
DIE WELT
- Around 20,000 people gather in Bonn to welcome Tour de France winner Jan Ullrich.
- Federal Labour Office president Bernhard Jagoda announces dramatic reduction in number of available apprenticeships.
